prompt_used:
I want to become a Mobile App Developer (Android / iOS) (Software Engineering). I have 5 months to prepare and I can study 3 hours per day. 
My experience level is University Final year CSE student. need a fast job. Basic (Completed some courses / small exercises) coding experience, familiar with only C Language.preferable language is C
Now generate a learning plan for me.

generated_plan.plan_title: Accelerated Mobile App Developer (Android/iOS via Cross-Platform) Learning Plan
generated_plan.current_experience: University Final year CSE student, basic C coding, familiar with CS fundamentals.
key_recommendations: Shift from C to modern mobile languages: Kotlin for Android and Dart for Flutter (cross-platform). While C provides a strong foundation in CS, it is not used for native Android/iOS development.
Prioritize practical project building. A strong portfolio on GitHub is crucial for a fast job.

Focus primarily on Android (Kotlin) initially to build a solid native foundation, then transition to Flutter to quickly achieve 'both Android/iOS' capability with less effort than learning native iOS from scratch.
Allocate significant time to algorithm practice and interview preparation in the final month.

topics: Introduction to Kotlin: Syntax, variables, data types, control flow, functions.
Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) in Kotlin: Classes, objects, inheritance, interfaces, abstraction, polymorphism.
Basic Data Structures & Algorithms in Kotlin: Arrays, Lists, Maps, Stacks, Queues, Sorting/Searching.
Introduction to Git and GitHub for version control.
IDE Familiarization: IntelliJ IDEA / Android Studio.
projects_and_exercises: Small console applications (e.g., calculator, simple text-based game).
Implement basic data structures and algorithms in Kotlin.

topics: Android Studio Setup & Project Structure.
XML Layouts: LinearLayout, RelativeLayout, ConstraintLayout (focus on ConstraintLayout).
Basic UI Elements: TextView, EditText, Button, ImageView.
Activities & their Lifecycle.
Event Handling (click listeners, input).
RecyclerView for displaying lists.
Fragments for modular UI.
Navigation Components for app flow.
projects_and_exercises: Create a layout with various UI elements.
Develop a multi-screen app using Activities and Navigation Components.
Build a 'To-Do List' app using RecyclerView.

topics: Data Storage: Shared Preferences (simple key-value), Room Persistence Library (SQLite database).
Networking: Introduction to Retrofit for REST API calls.
JSON Parsing: GSON/Moshi libraries.
Asynchronous Programming: Kotlin Coroutines.
MVVM Architecture: ViewModel, LiveData.
Basic Dependency Injection (e.g., using Hilt/Koin basics or manual DI).
projects_and_exercises: Refactor your 'To-Do List' app to use Room database.
Develop a 'Weather App' fetching data from a public API (e.g., OpenWeatherMap) using Retrofit and Coroutines.
Build a 'Movie/Book List' app displaying items from an API and allowing local favorites using Room.

monthly_breakdown.focus: Introduction to Cross-Platform (Flutter & Dart) for iOS/Android
topics: Introduction to Flutter: Why Flutter, advantages for 'both' platforms.
Dart Language Basics: Syntax, variables, functions, classes (quick transition from Kotlin).
Flutter Widgets: Stateless vs. Stateful, common UI widgets (Text, Button, Image, ListView, Row, Column).
Layouts in Flutter: Understanding the widget tree.
Navigation and Routing in Flutter.
State Management in Flutter (e.g., Provider or Bloc basics).
Networking in Flutter: HTTP package for API calls.
Data Persistence in Flutter: shared_preferences or sqflite.
projects_and_exercises: Build a simple 'Hello World' Flutter app.
Re-build your 'To-Do List' app using Flutter to understand differences and similarities.
Develop a simple 'Quote of the Day' app fetching data from an API using Flutter.

monthly_breakdown.focus: Advanced Flutter, Portfolio Building & Job Preparation
topics: Advanced Flutter: Custom Widgets, Animations, Platform Channels (brief overview).
Testing Basics in Flutter.
Improving UI/UX of existing projects.
Refining GitHub portfolio: Clean code, detailed READMEs, clear commit messages.
Resume/CV Preparation: Tailoring for mobile developer roles.
Interview Preparation: Common technical questions (DSA, OOP, Mobile-specific).
Understanding app deployment processes (Google Play Store, Apple App Store - high-level overview).
Networking: LinkedIn profile optimization, connecting with developers.
projects_and_exercises: Build a new, more complex Flutter app (e.g., a simple E-commerce app, social feed).
Polish 2-3 strongest portfolio projects (at least one native Android, at least one Flutter).
Practice coding challenges (e.g., LeetCode easy/medium) relevant to mobile/general SWE roles.
Create a personal developer blog or articles about your learning journey.

job_preparation_strategy: **Portfolio is King:** Have at least 2-3 well-documented, functional apps on GitHub (1 native Android, 1-2 Flutter). These demonstrate your skills more than any certificate.
**Algorithm Practice:** While not directly mobile dev, DSA questions are common in general SWE interviews. Solve easy/medium LeetCode problems.
**Interview Skills:** Practice explaining your projects, problem-solving approaches, and common mobile development concepts.
**Networking:** Leverage your university's career services, attend virtual meetups, and connect with professionals on LinkedIn.
**Customized Resume:** Tailor your resume for each job application, highlighting relevant skills and projects.
**Understand the Market:** Research companies hiring junior mobile developers and their typical tech stacks.
important_considerations: Your C language background provides a solid foundation in computer science principles, which will be very beneficial. However, for native mobile development, you must transition to languages like Kotlin (Android) and Swift (iOS). We recommend Kotlin and Dart (for Flutter) as they are modern and highly in demand.
Three hours a day is a good consistent effort. Maximize hands-on coding time over passive learning.
Stay updated with official documentation (Android Developers, Flutter.dev).
Don't be afraid to make mistakes; debugging is a crucial skill for developers.
This plan focuses on becoming proficient enough to land a junior role. Continuous learning is essential in this fast-evolving field.
